topics.name: Polite requests and offers (May I, Could you, Will you, Shall I)
Countable and uncountable nouns (many/much, few/little, fewer/less)

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: The student is study in his room now.
The student is studying in his room now.
The student studying in his room now.
questions.rule: Present continuous = is/am/are + -ing: is studying.

options: A train is fast than a horse.
A train is faster than a horse.
A train is more faster than a horse.
questions.rule: Comparing two things: fast becomes faster + than. Never say more faster.

options: Good evening, may I come in?
Good evening, may I comes in?
Good evening, may I coming in?
questions.rule: May I + base verb: May I come in?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Fall is irregular. Its simple past is fell.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: much ... than compares two people, so use the comparative: taller.
Books can be counted, so use many.

questions.after: you answer a question for me?
questions.rule: Will you + base verb ...? is a request: Will you answer ...?
A simple statement: subject + is + place.

chat: What are you doing, young man?
options: I am study for my exam.
I am studying for my exam.
questions.rule: Answer in the same tense as the question: I am studying.

options: Thank you. You is very kind.
Thank you. You are very kind.
Thanks you. You are very kind.
questions.rule: Say Thank you (or Thanks), and you takes are.

options: Today, less people die of illness.
Today, fewer people dies of illness.
Today, fewer people die of illness.
questions.rule: People can be counted, so use fewer. People is plural: die.

options: Books are cheaper today than in the past.
Books are more cheap today than in the past.
Books are cheapest today than in the past.
questions.rule: Short adjective + -er + than: cheaper than.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Yesterday shows the past, so use the simple past: visited.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: People can be counted, so ask How many.
The + -est picks one out of all: the fastest.

questions.after: on horseback or in a coach.
questions.rule: In Newton's time is the past, so use travelled.
Ask for permission with May I + base verb ...?
Fewer goes before a countable plural noun: fewer students.

chat: Which is faster, the bus or the metro?
questions.rule: Comparing two things, use the comparative: faster.

chat: Rohan, the window is open and it is cold.
options: Shall I close the window, ma'am?
Shall I closing the window, ma'am?
Shall I to close the window, ma'am?
questions.rule: To offer help, use Shall I + base verb ...?

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tenses.
options: The student was studying when Newton knocked at the door.
The student was studying when Newton knock at the door.
The student studying when Newton knocked at the door.
questions.rule: Longer action: was studying. Short action that broke in: knocked.

options: There is less traffic in the morning.
There are less traffic in the morning.
There is fewer traffic in the morning.
questions.rule: Traffic cannot be counted: use is and less.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Good is irregular: good, better, best.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Simple future = will + base verb: will tell.

questions.after: time travelling than people did long ago.
questions.rule: Time here cannot be counted, so use less, not fewer.

questions.after: I ask you one more question?
questions.rule: Ask for permission with may I + base verb.
Present continuous question: What + are + you + -ing?
Happy becomes happier (y changes to i + er) before than.

chat: How many apples are left in the basket?
questions.rule: Apples can be counted, so use a few, with the plural verb are.

chat: Did you watch the film about Newton?
options: Yes, I watched it last night.
Yes, I watch it last night.
Yes, I watching it last night.
questions.rule: Last night is the past, so use the simple past: watched.

options: Newton was one of the greatest scientists of his time.
Newton was one of the greatest scientist of his time.
Newton was one of the most great scientists of his time.
questions.rule: One of the + superlative + plural noun: one of the greatest scientists.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tenses.
options: The student throw his books on the floor and offered Newton a chair.
The student threw his books on the floor and offer Newton a chair.
The student threw his books on the floor and offered Newton a chair.
questions.rule: Both actions are in the past: threw and offered.

options: Could you tells me the way to the library?
Could you tell me the way to the library?
Could you telling me the way to the library?
questions.rule: Could you + base verb: Could you tell me ...?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Milk cannot be counted, so use a little, not a few.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: One person in the past continuous takes was: was sleeping.
Long adjectives use more ... than: more plentiful than.
Look out! means it is happening right now: present continuous is falling.
Time cannot be counted, so ask How much time.

chat: Thank you for answering so many questions.
questions.rule: A negative request is don't + base verb: Please don't mention it.

chat: Is the new phone better than your old one?
options: Yes, it is much more better.
questions.rule: Make a comparative stronger with much: much better. Never more better or very better.

options: Fewer people travel by coach today, and they spend less time on the road.
Less people travel by coach today, and they spend less time on the road.
Fewer people travel by coach today, and they spend fewer time on the road.
questions.rule: Fewer with things you count (people); less with things you cannot count (time).

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tenses.
options: If we will use less time for travelling, we will have more time for other things.
If we use less time for travelling, we will have more time for other things.
If we use less time for travelling, we had more time for other things.
questions.rule: If + simple present, then will + base verb: If we use ..., we will have ...

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Of all compares more than two things, so use the superlative: the most useful.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Will you please + base verb: answer.

questions.after: people who still travel on horseback today.
questions.rule: People can be counted: use few. Much and less go with things you cannot count.

questions.after: to measure than speed or weight.
questions.rule: Comparing with than needs the comparative: harder. Hardly means 'almost not'.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence in the past continuous.
questions.rule: Past continuous: was + -ing; the student's room = the room of the student.
Polite request: Could you + base verb + me + thing?

chat: What will people do with the extra time?
options: They will spends it on things they enjoy.
They spending it on things they enjoy.
They will spend it on things they enjoy.
questions.rule: A will question gets a will answer: will spend (base verb after will).

chat: Did you find any information about Newton's life?
options: Yes, I found a little information.
Yes, I found a few informations.
Yes, I found a few information.
questions.rule: Information cannot be counted: no -s, and use a little, not a few.
